verifications.note: OG&E application to ODEQ for River Valley Generating Station, Le Flore County. It proposes five GE 7F.05 gas simple-cycle turbines of about 224.8 MW each, about 1,124 MW, or two combined-cycle blocks, to replace the coal units.

records.action: Add one new gas unit group of five simple-cycle turbines at the existing River Valley plant, pre-construction.
records.note:
GEM lists only the two coal units here. OG&E has applied for a construction permit to add five GE 7F.05 gas turbines of about 224.8 MW each, so a new unit is proposed. The owner is OG&E, the applicant.

Where to find it:
- Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality application for River Valley, updated March 10, 2026, original submission March 27, 2025 (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/Af6FiOuAWfwTfP7%C3%89lBObAZu2%C3%81jK627i0ruRb1YVA9ucGjOJwUUHCsEMbR%C3%81V4w%C3%819YC3Cw0VwM4maTrcJLCxoanak%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true). Page 9 of the PDF, printed Page 1 of 29, 1. Introduction. Scenario 1 is five GE 7F.05 simple-cycle turbines at "approximately 224.8 MW each", about 1,124 MW in total. Scenario 2 is two GE 7HA.03 turbines at about 449 MW each in 1x1 combined cycle, about 640 MW per block, about 1,280 MW in total. OG&E proposes to retire the four existing boilers. The facility operates under Permit No. 2016-0355-TVR2 (M-2).
- Page 1 is a March 10, 2026 email from OG&E amending the application to add the second scenario. Pages 11 to 12 list the 7F.05 at about 224.8 MW, with a typical operating output of about 213 MW, and the emission units 3-B-01 through 3-B-05.
- EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx). Plant ID 10671 lists only coal generators GEN1 and GEN2, so no gas unit exists yet.
- Southwest Power Pool open queue list (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV), row GEN-2024-286. Nearest Town is La Flore, TO at POI is OGE, Fuel Type is Gas, Substation or Line is AES 5 161 kV Substation, Status is DISIS STAGE, Request Received 3/1/2025.

Why this differs:
- In row GEN-2024-286 the Nameplate Capacity column says 496 and the Capacity column says 136. The permit total is larger, so the permit capacity is used and the mismatch is flagged in a question.
- The new unit is named 3 because GEM already lists units 1 and 2. The five turbines are one unit group of five engines.

Not found:
- The permit number 2025-0187 does not appear anywhere in the text of the application when I read it again. I cannot confirm that number from this source.

verifications.note: SPP surplus study report for GEN-2025-SR9. It describes 20 INDAR and Ingeteam synchronous gas-fired units of 21.0812 MW each, 421.6 MW in all at the Muskogee 345 kilovolt substation, shared with Muskogee units 4, 5 and 6 (1,908 MW), limited to 400 MW of injection.
SPP active queue list updated November 3, 2026. Row GEN-2025-SR9: Fort Gibson, OG&E area, 400 MW, IA PENDING.

records.note:
GEM has the plant but not this unit. A Southwest Power Pool surplus study describes about 421.6 MW of gas engines at the Muskogee substation, so a new unit is proposed with status announced. The owner is left blank for the reviewer.

Where to find it:
- Southwest Power Pool surplus interconnection impact study for GEN-2025-SR9 (https://opsportal.spp.org/documents/studies/files/2025_Generation_Studies/FINAL_SPP_Report_GEN-2025-SR9_06112026.pdf). Page 5 of the PDF, Executive Summary, Table ES-1, row GEN-2025-SR9 gives Interconnection Queue Capacity 400. The row for Muskogee Units 4, 5, and 6 gives 1908.
- Page 5 also says "20 x INDAR/Ingeteam synchronous gas-fired units operating at 21.0812 MW for a total assumed dispatch of 421.624 MW". Injection is limited to 400 MW at the point of interconnection, and the combined generation may not exceed 1908 MW.
- Page 6, the point of interconnection table, reads "Muskogee 345 kV (515224)" and "20 x INDAR/Ingeteam 21.0812 MW (Thermal) = 421.624 [dispatch]".
- Open queue list (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GenerateActiveCSV), row GEN-2025-SR9. Nearest Town is Fort Gibson. TO at POI is OG&E. Capacity is 400. Nameplate Capacity is 0. Commercial Operation Date is 12/1/2029. Status is IA PENDING. Substation or Line is Muskogee 345 KV Substation.

Why this differs:
- The injection is capped at 400 MW, but the equipment adds up to 421.6 MW. The listed capacity is the equipment total. The interconnection agreement is still pending, so the status is announced.

Owner:
- The queue list and the study do not name the company behind the request. OG&E owns the existing units at this substation, but a surplus request can come from a different company. So no owner is assumed. No regulator filing or news item naming one was found.

Engine type:
- The study says synchronous gas-fired units and names INDAR and Ingeteam, but no engine model. The engine type is read from the unit size and count.

records.note:

records.researcher_notes:
The Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority has applied for a construction permit for one new 90 MW GE 7E.03 simple cycle turbine at its Lamb plant in Ponca City. The permit is still in technical review, so the status stays pre-construction.

Where to find it:
- Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality application, May 28, 2026 (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/Ac%C3%89PChnKuUSvuWZVQIFTvlUUq5X%C3%81Hzd9Glajj%C3%89H9yC3L05C3YHBOqpbheH2tQFiUXhjxRQlq2n6qKEna9J83FQI%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true). Page 3 of the PDF, the cover letter from the Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority, 4250 W. Doolin Avenue, Ponca City, Kay County, says the permit "will allow OMPA to install one 90MW General Electric 7E.03 simple cycle natural gas combustion turbine".
- Page 7, "1.1 Project Description", says one 90-megawatt General Electric 7E.03. Page 10 lists EU 2 as the "90-MW General Electric 7E.03". Page 16, Part 3, EUG description, EU ID# 2, shows Construction/Modification Date 2028.
- Completeness notice and proof of publication (https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/Aa4uMQdC7sAIwdopO3DGmSJ1fN6dFuZ2DF2LgcWnu1nPjwUZQst2jzAUeBwyDm8c3sU6S71OwLno%C3%81pg5HeNZltE%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true). Page 1 of the PDF is a letter dated June 16, 2026, titled "Proof of Publication" for the notice of filing a construction permit application for New Unit 2, Permit Number 2020-0434-C (M-1). It says that on June 8, 2026 the Department issued a notice that the application submitted May 29, 2026 was administratively complete, and that the notice ran in the Ponca City News on June 11, 2026. Pages 3 and 4 hold the June 8 and June 16 emails with the completeness letter.

Why this differs:
- The application gives 2028 as the construction date, so 2028 is used as the start year.
- The Southwest Power Pool request GEN-2024-334 is this unit. The open queue list (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive) shows GEN-2024-334 as 103 MW of gas in Kay County at the Ranch Road 345 kV substation, study cluster DISIS-2024-001, commercial operation June 1, 2029. The Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority board minutes of August 8, 2024 (https://www.ompa.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/August-Board-Minutes-2024.pdf), page 5, item 13, authorize staff to submit a generation interconnection request with the Southwest Power Pool "in the approximate amount of 103MW" for the new Lamb unit before the October 31 deadline. The 124 MW figure comes from the October 2024 minutes, page 6, which say "We are going into the queue at 124 MW, which are the 2 Siemens units." The permit now names one GE turbine instead. Lamb's existing turbine connects on the same Rose Hill to Sooner 345 kV line (request GEN-2012-041). No other gas request in Kay County fits. The permit figure of 90 MW is the manufacturer rating and is used here. The September 2025 minutes, page 4, item 12, say the turbines would not be delivered until 2029, so the operating year may be 2029 rather than 2028. The ompa.com site refused every connection later on November 6, 2026, so the minutes are named here but not added as a Data Source.
